top3.headline: Kloss: audit agent skills with rival models, keep edits they agree on
top3.whyItMatters: Teams can refresh agent instructions per model release without trusting any single model's edits.

top3.headline: mod_wsgi's author builds a Rust server for Python apps with AI
top3.whyItMatters: Seasoned engineers now use AI for production infrastructure, not just prototypes.

top3.headline: Meng To open-sources three skills for Liquid Glass and 3D interfaces
top3.whyItMatters: Reusable design skills make polished interactive interfaces cheaper to prototype.

items.title: Meng To open-sources three skills for Liquid Glass and 3D interfaces
items.takeaway: He says GPT 6.2 Astra rebuilt a desk scene in three.js with interactive objects. He published skills for liquid glass, press shaders and a 3D room.
items.soWhat: Design teams can reuse packaged skills instead of prompting rich interfaces from scratch.

items.title: Kloss: audit agent skills with rival models, keep edits they agree on
items.takeaway: Two Cursor cloud agents run read-only audits of his skills with Gemini 4 Neon and Fable 5.2; he applies only agreed edits. They agreed on 22 of 104 skills.
items.soWhat: Skills written for older models drift, and a consensus check is a cheap way to update them.

items.title: Simon Willison flags Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for Python apps
items.takeaway: Graham Dumpleton, author of mod_wsgi, built Muru with AI help to run ASGI and WSGI apps, documenting it in detail over three weeks.
items.soWhat: A veteran maintainer shipping production infrastructure with AI is stronger proof than a demo.

image.alt: Simon Willison: Simon Willison flags Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for Python apps

items.title: Musk shows real-time AI video with no game engine
items.takeaway: He posts a demo of real-time AI video generation, 'no gaming engine', running on half of one AI4 TRIP accelerator. The claim is his and not independently verified.
items.soWhat: Unverified, but real-time generated video on small hardware would change interactive media costs.

items.title: Theo: a DeepMind Antigravity engineer is improving Gemini in T3 Code
items.takeaway: He says a DeepMind engineer who works on Antigravity has landed many PRs to improve Gemini support in T3 Code, calling it 'as official as it gets'.
items.soWhat: Google engineers are helping a third-party coding tool support Gemini, not only Google's own apps.

items.title: Harrison Chase: buying Copilot alone does not change how teams work
items.takeaway: He says many companies buy Copilot or similar tools and wonder why AI isn't changing how their team works. He calls a 'knowledge factory' the missing piece and links an article.
items.soWhat: Licenses are not adoption; ask what system turns your team's work into reusable knowledge.

items.title: Perplexity moves some Computer Teammates to Gemini Neon
items.takeaway: Aravind Srinivas says Gemini Neon on high reasoning is intelligent and fast. He has migrated some of his Perplexity Computer Teammates to it.
items.soWhat: Model switching is now routine; keep your agents portable across providers.

items.title: Simon Willison: Gemini 4 xhigh effort cost 23.61 cents, not 3.99
items.takeaway: On his pelican test, Gemini 4 Hydrogen used 31,477 output tokens on xhigh effort versus 5,311 on high. Cost rose from 3.99 to 23.61 cents.
items.soWhat: Set thinking effort per task; the top setting can multiply token spend several times over.

items.title: Matt Pocock: teach an agent your style by scoring its sentences
items.takeaway: He proposes a small scorer app: the agent sends example sentences and you rate them one at a time, swipe-style, either 1-4 or by picking between options.
items.soWhat: Quick human ratings may be a cheap way to give an agent your own voice.

items.title: a16z: Navan bookings doubled after the Nov 13 FAA ground stop
items.takeaway: a16z's Chart of the Week shows Navan car and hotel bookings spiking to roughly twice normal hourly volume after the November 13 FAA ground stop.
items.soWhat: Booking demand can double within hours of a disruption; travel systems must absorb it.

items.title: Meng To lists motion skills for animating UI with agents
items.takeaway: He points to HyperFrames, which renders video from HTML with agents, Emil Kowalski's animation skills, and DesignBookmark Motion animated components.
items.soWhat: Agents can now add motion to interfaces through ready-made skills.

items.title: Thinking Machines publishes Inkling 2 Mini
items.takeaway: Thinking Machines posted Inkling 2 Mini on its news page. A separate Hacker News post shows it running in 5.4 GB of memory.
items.soWhat: Watch whether small models that fit modest hardware cut inference costs for routine work.

image.alt: Thinking Machines: Thinking Machines publishes Inkling 2 Mini

items.title: Paper: language models can rewrite their own weights
items.takeaway: An arXiv paper, 'Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights', drew 487 points on Hacker News.
items.soWhat: Self-updating models would make testing and governance harder, so track whether the result replicates.
